question: What did enslaved people in the British Caribbean get when slavery was abolished in 1834?
answer: More unpaid work. Under the 1833 Act, most freed people over six became apprentices, bound to work up to 45 hours a week for their former owners, without wages, for four to six more years. The owners received £20 million, about 40% of the Treasury's yearly income. Protest ended apprenticeship early, in 1838.
move: Read the transition clauses before celebrating the date a law took effect.
ask: Before I cheer a new rule or promise, have I read what it really changes on day one?
reference: Draper, The Price of Emancipation: Slave-Ownership, Compensation and British Slave Society at the End of Slavery, Cambridge University Press, 2010
